prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right agency depends on your goals, budget, industry, timeline and whether you need SEO, PPC, social, content, analytics, creative, or full-funnel growth. I can help find the best fit, but I need a few details first.

Quick questions
- What are your top goals? (e.g., brand awareness, lead generation, e‑commerce revenue, app installs)
- Primary channels you care about? (SEO, paid search, social ads, content, email, CRO, analytics)
- Monthly/annual budget range for agency fees + ad spend?
- Company stage/size and industry (startup, SMB, enterprise; B2B or B2C; SaaS, marketplace, retail, health, etc.)
- Prefer local SF agency vs. remote/national? Agency size preference (boutique vs. large)?
- Timeline for results or campaign start?

How I can help next
- If you give the answers above I’ll shortlist 3–5 San Francisco agencies matched to your needs (with strengths, pricing ballpark, and relevant case examples).
- If you want to self-research, check Clutch.co, G2, Google Partners, and LinkedIn for SF agencies and filter by reviews and industry experience.

Quick checklist to evaluate agencies
- Relevant case studies (same industry or similar KPIs)
- Measurable results (CPA, ROAS, MQLs, revenue) — not just vanity metrics
- Clear strategy and process (discovery, testing, optimization cycle)
- Reporting cadence & dashboards (what metrics, who sees them)
- Team make-up and senior involvement (will senior strategists work on your account?)
- Tools & tech stack (analytics, tracking, automation)
- Pricing model and minimum commitment/contract terms
- References from clients with similar goals

Would you like me to shortlist agencies now? If yes, answer the quick questions above (or tell me one key requirement) and I’ll return 3–5 recommended SF agencies with a brief rationale for each.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
